$meta.description: Semantic color palette extracted from the VS Code theme's raw hex values, deduplicated and named by role rather than by UI widget. Intended as a portable base for applying the same look to other, unrelated designs.
$meta.character: Dark violet ground with a warm coral/orange primary accent and a spread of saturated neon secondaries (cyan, teal, mint, lavender, amber, rose) used for variety/data-viz.

void.use: deepest background — outer chrome, borders-of-borders, shadow tint

raised.use: raised surface — hover states, secondary buttons, panels

elevated.use: highest elevation — active/selected surface, tooltips, popovers

subtle.use: low-contrast structural lines (indent guides, whitespace glyphs)

onAccent.use: text/icons placed on top of accent-filled surfaces

primary.use: primary brand accent — links, focus rings, active states, cursor

primaryDeep.use: primary accent, deep/low-luminance variant — filled button backgrounds, badges

secondary.use: secondary warm accent (kept from the original orange theme) — numeric/constant emphasis, debug states

usageNotes: Backgrounds get darker/flatter toward 'void'; content/interactive elements get lighter and more saturated toward 'elevated' and 'accent'.
accent.primary (#AE50FE) is the single most-reused color in the source theme — treat it as THE brand color: CTAs, focus states, active nav, links.

accent.primaryDeep (#7209B7) is a purple derived to match the new primary's hue at the same depth the original A32605 sat relative to the old orange — use it wherever a filled/pressed state of the primary accent is needed.

accent.secondary (#FF580C) is the one color deliberately left orange — a nod to the theme's original accent, now reading as a distinct warm counterpoint to the purple primary rather than a competing brand color.
The syntax set reads as a cohesive 'neon on violet' rainbow — good for tags, category chips, chart series, or status dots where you need many distinct-but-harmonious hues.
state.* colors are WCAG AA-verified against surface.base/canvas in the source theme — safe to reuse directly for error/warning/info/success UI on a dark violet ground.
For a light-mode counterpart, this theme package also ships 'Satellite Daybreak' (satellite-daybreak.json) — ask if you want that palette extracted too.
